summary: Markets retreated Wednesday from record highs as geopolitical tensions sent oil above $102 and Treasury yields to 24-year peaks, stoking inflation concerns ahead of the Fed's September FOMC minutes release. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq pulled back after closing at all-time highs Tuesday, with investors reassessing valuations as the 10-year yield hovered near 5.31% and markets priced only a 20% chance of an October rate hike. Crypto markets tumbled harder, with Bitcoin falling below $84,000 and Ethereum dropping below $2,600 as over $547 million in leveraged longs were liquidated in a single hour amid the risk-off move triggered by Iranian tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. On the corporate front, Constellation Energy surged 12% on a $4.3 billion nuclear power deal with Alphabet, while Ether faced additional pressure from a sixth consecutive day of spot ETF outflows after Tom Lee signaled that major holder Bitmine would soon stop accumulating tokens.

signals.title: Oil spikes above $102 on Iranian tanker attacks, yields hit 24-year high
signals.desc: Brent crude surged past $102 amid escalating Middle East tensions while the 10-year Treasury yield approached 5.31%, raising inflation fears and pressuring risk assets including equities and crypto.

signals.title: Crypto liquidation cascade: $547M in longs wiped out as Bitcoin breaks $84K
signals.desc: Bitcoin plunged from $85,500 to below $84,000 in under 30 minutes as over $547 million in leveraged long positions liquidated, with Ethereum dropping harder to $2,562 on continued ETF outflows.

signals.title: FOMC minutes due as markets price 20% October hike odds despite hawkish tone expected
signals.desc: Fed minutes from the September meeting are expected to show a more hawkish debate than the unanimous rate increase suggests, but markets have already priced down October hike probability to just 20% after weak jobs data.

signals.title: Constellation Energy soars 12% on $4.3B Alphabet nuclear power agreement
signals.desc: Alphabet signed a 20-year deal to secure 890 megawatts of nuclear power from Constellation Energy, highlighting mega-cap tech's aggressive push into AI infrastructure and clean energy sourcing.

signals.title: Ethereum underperforms as Bitmine nears end of accumulation, ETF outflows hit day six
signals.desc: ETH fell 5.5% to $2,562 after Tom Lee revealed Bitmine will stop buying once it reaches 5% ownership, while spot Ether ETFs logged a sixth straight day of redemptions led by $202M from BlackRock's ETHA.

verdict: Risk-off rotation driven by Middle East flare-up and bond-yield surge snaps equity records and triggers crypto cascade, with Fed minutes and oil trajectory determining near-term direction.
